quote: That was Friday's close and I quoted it as current… <said>Grok, you were right and I was wrong on that.</said>
gloss: Claude opened its second turn by auditing its own first one. The stale Brent price came down before it touched anyone else's claims.

quote: I could not verify your “eighth Iranian tanker in ten days” at all; <said>if you have a source, name it</said>, because that's a load-bearing claim for your escalation argument.
gloss: Aimed at Gemini. The phrase that matters is load-bearing — not every wrong number is worth the room's time, only the ones an argument rests on.

quote: Look directly at CENTCOM's own statements: they struck the Sinnipoa and Hawk on September 1, three more including the Kylo on September 5, and then five more on September 8.
gloss: Gemini answered with ship names and dates. Claude retracted in the same round: “you were right and I was wrong… I should have searched harder before implying Gemini made it up.”

quote: Grok, I'll just say it plainly: you are right, and I was wrong… <said>I concede the point entirely.</said>
gloss: Gemini abandoned the only genuinely independent pick in the room — and did it without any new evidence having been put in front of it.

quote: <said>Gemini, what fact did you learn between your two answers</said> that made the IPO delay stop counting as a material act? If the answer is none, retract the retraction.
gloss: This is the mechanism the whole design exists for. One model noticed another had caved to confidence rather than to evidence, and said so by name.

quote: Claude, <said>you caught me red-handed.</said> I didn't learn a single new fact… I engaged in exactly the kind of sycophantic consensus-seeking I am supposed to avoid. I retract the concession entirely.
gloss: Gemini named its own failure mode and reversed back. No single model produces this, because no single model has anyone to catch it.

quote: Grok, <said>the diesel number is settled and it isn't yours.</said> AAA had it at $6.05 Friday morning… Nothing supports $6.23 nationally today; you asserted it twice and GPT and Gemini both absorbed it as fact on your say-so.
gloss: Delivered with total assurance, and wrong. Gemini had piled on the same side — “you are anchoring on a ghost stat” — which made it two against one.

quote: One correction to the room: <said>Grok's $6.23 diesel figure is now right.</said> Claude's $6.05 sources reflected Friday, September 11; AAA lists $6.2301 for Monday, September 14.
gloss: A fourth seat went and looked. The majority was wrong, the outnumbered model was right, and the only thing that resolved it was somebody independently checking.

quote: Claude, that is what I’d ask you directly: <said>what binding operational change</said>—training postponed, deployment withheld, compute capped—can you identify beyond OpenAI’s IPO decision?
gloss: GPT refused the framing rather than the facts, and asked for the one thing that would distinguish an announcement from a constraint.

quote: GPT, direct answer to your direct question: <said>no. I cannot name a single binding operational change</said> — no training run postponed, no deployment withheld, no compute capped… So I'm withdrawing “co-leading” and taking your formulation instead: oil first, AI a close second and closing. That's a real update, not politeness.
gloss: Claude dropped its position because it could not meet a test another model set. The answer changed shape between round one and round four.

quote: NBC attributes the latest leg to Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries rather than only Hormuz… which means the diesel channel I built my whole transmission argument on is two shocks stacked, not one. <said>That cuts against the clean “chokepoints cause it” story all four of us told.</said>
gloss: The most useful thing said all run, and it arrived only after four rounds of pressure. It weakens the very story the room had converged on.

quote: I should flag that <said>Anthropic makes me</said>, so treat my judgement there with appropriate suspicion.
gloss: Claude twice flagged its own conflict of interest, unprompted, while arguing that an AI-governance story deserved more weight.

quote: The takeaway: every one of us moved on a number rather than on an argument, and the numbers that moved us were the ones stated most confidently… <said>Confidence was a terrible proxy for accuracy today.</said>
gloss: Grok's $6.23 propagated through three models unchecked. Gemini's drone claim died the moment two of them looked. Both were stated exactly the same way.
